title: Partyet 1721 (catalogue 541): the French consul at Cadiz to the Conseil de Marine, 7 April 1721, cipher passage read

steps.what: Register AE/B/I/226 found digitised in the AN virtual inventory room (images AE-B-I-226_009-341).
Table rebuilt from the contemporary interlinear decipherments of five neighbouring Partyet letters; frozen.
Frozen table on held-out glossed letters (Jan-Feb 1721): ~235 covered numbers, 0 disagreements.
77 groups read; 392 = service from the phrase and the alphabetical block of s- words.
OCR sweep of glossed cipher letters 1717-1730 (AE/B/I/223-240): 392 = service in three glosses (1725, 1730).

outcome.method_basis: Table rebuilt from contemporary decipherments of sibling letters in the same register, validated on held-out glossed letters.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 35/35 words read in their sense; 33 certain (94%), 2 probable (dernie{r}, déci{dé}: ends in the binding); 392 = service attested in glossed letters of 1725 and 1730.

credits.note: table rebuilt from sibling glosses, validated on held-out letters; passage read, English translation

texts.label: Partyet to the Conseil de Marine, Cadiz, 7 April 1721 (cipher passage)
texts.summary: It is said that the latter does not act as he should for the good of the service; to be decided shortly, both sides having written to Madrid.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 31 Oct 2026: the 35-word cipher passage is one coherent sentence pair joining the clear text on both sides; two endings lost in the binding, no hole.

prior.where: Inventory says "non transcrite"; catalogue 541 open (checked 28 Oct 2026).

human: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
